public_rationale: The mid-April 2024 production account describes missing controls for matching characters across shots, different outputs from repeated prompts, and unwanted changes to the balloon character [e1]. This supports the contextual claim that the contemporary Sora preview could not reliably deliver intended, consistent movie scenes [e1]. The account published May 8, 2024 documents a completed music video using about 55 of roughly 700 generated clips, with some transitions handled in After Effects [e2]. That demonstrates useful footage and a completed project, but does not establish reliable control of intended scenes [e2].
limitations: The accounts do not establish that Sora was unusable for every movie-making purpose.
There is no matched production test or agreed threshold separating ordinary post-production from substantial corrective work.
The evidence concerns preview workflows within April 1–May 13, 2024, not later Sora versions.

our_interpretation: The ordinary contextual reading concerns Sora's usefulness for making directed, consistent movie scenes, rather than whether it can produce any usable footage.
Ordinary editing and color grading do not establish failure. Repeatedly changing the intended scene or repairing unwanted content is relevant evidence of a workflow limitation.
The speaker supplies no reporting period. I use the latest completed month and the elapsed publication month, April 1 through May 13, 2024, for the ongoing preview workflow.
The phrase about making a movie specifies the use case; it is not a conditional forecast.

criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented professional movie production demonstrates that the contemporary Sora workflow reliably delivered intended, consistent scenes with ordinary production work.
